subject: Additional arrival when start_time is not zero

messages.author: 89fbf1eb7aa54f21
messages.subject: Additional arrival when start_time is not zero
parts:
Hi Iñaki,

First of all thank you so much for sharing Simmer with everyone, the package is great!

While trying to recover an experimentally observed arrival distribution (which changes according to the hour of the day), I noticed that the generators I was joining were having what looks like an additional event right before the 'start_time' int the 'from_to' function.  I tried reproducing the issue in this minimalistic example:

bank <-
  simmer() %>%
  add_generator("Customer",
                trajectory("Customer's path"),
                from_to(start_time = 0,
                        stop_time = 60,
                        arrive = FALSE,
                        dist = function() { -1 }))


bank %>% run() %>% get_mon_arrivals()

> [1] name          start_time    end_time      activity_time finished    
> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

As expected, no arrivals take place. However, if start_time is larger than 0, there is one event right before start_time:

bank <-
  simmer() %>%
  add_generator("Customer",
                trajectory("Customer's path"),
                from_to(start_time = 10,
                        stop_time = 60,
                        arrive = FALSE,
                        dist = function() { -1 }))


bank %>% run() %>% get_mon_arrivals()

>        name start_time end_time activity_time finished replication
> 1 Customer0          9        9             0     TRUE           1


1. Is this a feature or a bug?
2. Is there a way to prevent it?  Currently I am joining 24 generators for each hour of the day, and get 23 additional arrivals, which compresses the dynamic range of the events I want to characterize.

Thank you!

gen()
#> [1] 9

generator to generate nothing). Could you please:

- open an issue on GitHub with both examples? (If you have an account
there; otherwise, I can do it myself).

Thanks for the report.

Thanks for your response, Iñaki. 

The need for a -1 to terminate a generator before it generates any arrivals comes when there are two or more generators joined consecutively in time. Let's say the first generator, gen1, has a low arrival rate and the second one, gen2, has a high arrival rate. If we always let one arrival from gen1 to take place, that arrival time will likely fall well within the gen2's [start_time, stop_time] range, potentially preempting many arrivals from the gen2.  To fix that, if an attempted arrival time from gen1 goes beyond start_time from gen2, I shut down gen1.

Does that make sense?

Here is the example:

set.seed(1)

interarrival_times_per_period <- c(300, 200, 3) # each period extends over 60 units
sim <- simmer()

inter_arrival_time <- function(period, env) {
  time_delta = rexp(1, 1/interarrival_times_per_period[period])
  print(paste("Period:", period, "tentative time_delta:", time_delta))
  mins_into_the_period = now(env) - period*60
  # terminate generator if tentative arrival is crosses into next generator's period
  ifelse(time_delta + mins_into_the_period > 60, -1, time_delta) 
}

a <- map(1:length(interarrival_times_per_period), 
         function(i) add_generator(sim, paste0("customer period", i), 
                trajectory(),
                from_to(start_time = i*60,
                        stop_time = (i + 1)*60 - 1,
                        arrive = FALSE,
                        dist = function() { inter_arrival_time(i, sim) })))

sim %>% run() %>% get_mon_arrivals()

To fix that, if an attempted arrival time from gen1 goes beyond start_time from gen2, I shut down gen1.
>

I don't understand why do you need to insert a -1. The whole purpose
of from_to is to automatically insert a -1 when the stop_time is
exceeded. E.g.:

gen <- from_to(4, 12, function() 3, FALSE)
gen()
#> [1] 7
gen()
#> [1] 3
gen()
#> [1] -1

Iñaki

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Additional arrival when start_time is not zero
parts:
Generators 'from', 'to' and 'from_to' are convenience functions to
start and/or stop the arrival process at specified times, so they are
not designed to cope with any -1 coming from the distribution
provided. Changing this behaviour complicates the design and does not
add any new functionality, so I think that the best solution is to add
a warning in the documentation about this.

Iñaki
